commit.message:
Render the repair metadata CoordError has always carried

Every CoordError in this crate carries four facts beyond its code and reason:
the purpose of the boundary that refused, at least two concrete fixes, a narrow
next step, and a repository-relative documentation anchor. repair_metadata fills
all four for every code, the anchors all resolve in docs/errors.md, and there is
a test asserting there are never fewer than two fixes.

None of it has ever reached an operator. Display writes "{code}: {reason}" and
nothing read the rest, so the only consumers of purpose, common_fixes, docs_url
and repair_hint were four assertions in the test suite. A person running the CLI
saw a bare token like UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA and had to read the source to find out
what to do about it. Now they see this:

    bullet-family: UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA
      family.lock schema 2 is not installable; retain it for diagnosis, regenerate schema 3 from authenticated signed tags, and replace it atomically

      protecting    reject a schema outside the admitted version set
      try           - follow the explicit export or removal procedure
                    - use the binary and lock version that own the subject
      next          follow the schema-removal or setup-recovery runbook
      docs          docs/errors.md#unsupported-or-corrupt-state

Display is untouched and always will be: it is the machine contract, a great
deal of tooling greps stderr for "CODE: reason", and the rendered form still
leads with the code on line one so those greps keep working. For the same reason
the reason text is never hard-wrapped. Wrapping it broke
release_profiles::ordinary_release_requires_an_explicit_profile, which greps for
a phrase that a newline had landed in the middle of. That failure was the useful
kind: it says exactly which text is a surface other people depend on. A terminal
soft-wraps a long line by itself at no cost, so only the metadata block, which
nothing greps because until now it was never printed, is laid out to a width.

One colour rule, in one place, with no new dependency. src/diagnostic.rs decides
once, from values passed in rather than looked up, so the rule is a pure function
with tests: NO_COLOR when present and non-empty, CLICOLOR_FORCE to paint a pipe,
a dumb or absent TERM never painted even when forced, and otherwise the depth the
terminal advertises. Three tiers, because a palette that emits truecolor
unconditionally is a bet rather than a palette. --no-color, --plain and
--color=<auto|always|never> are new and are stripped from argv before dispatch,
since colour is a property of the terminal and not of any command.

The 985-character single-line USAGE is now a grouped listing. Nothing asserted on
its exact text; tests/family_lock.rs asserted on one concatenated fragment of it,
and that assertion is now two assertions plus a negative one, which is stricter
than what it replaced: it would catch one verb's arguments drifting while the
other's did not.

Fold the width digits by hand, and format

Two hosted findings, both correct.

crates/bullet-wire/tests/canonical_hostile/metadata.rs inventories every `.parse(`
call in production Rust and admits exactly one, in bullet-wire's canonical
decoder, so that no other decode path can grow quietly. Reading COLUMNS through
str::parse added a second. A terminal width is not a reason to widen that
inventory, so the digits are folded explicitly instead. The replacement is also
the better code: it cannot panic and it cannot overflow, and it has a test that
says so, including a forty-digit input.

The rest is cargo fmt on the test helpers.

Index every document, and make the index a control instead of a habit

Fifty-four of ninety-one documents under docs/ were absent from docs/README.md,
including every one of the twenty decision records, every one of the twelve
runbooks and the entire spec directory. The index also named none of the operator
commands: zero mentions of bullet tui, bullet auth or bullet coding, for its first
three weeks, while those were already the primary way anyone touches this product.
Its "Last reviewed" line said 2026-08-25.

Curation is a habit and habits drift, so this adds the control rather than only
the content. tests/assurance_controls.rs walks docs/ and refuses when any tracked
Markdown document is not referenced by the index, naming the exact files. It also
asserts that every command the CLI exposes appears there. Removing one line from
the inventory now fails with

    1 of 90 documents under docs/ are absent from docs/README.md: runbooks/signer-rotation.md

bullet serve and bullet setup are deliberately NOT indexed. They are not merged,
and an index that named them would be claiming a command this tree does not have.

The new Operator surface table pairs each command with the document that is
authority for it, and states the one colour rule the rest of this branch
implements. Every link resolves: ops/ci/check-links.sh passes over 92 files.
